empirical_claims.note: The authors' own figures, quoted verbatim from the arXiv abstract (each quote is an exact substring of the abstract). Not checked, reproduced or re-claimed by this sketch. They appear only in this file.

claims.about: the upstream is an agent runtime with a control plane; this sketch does not port it
claims.quote: We present Synapse-Control, an agent runtime whose lightweight control plane selects advice and determines when to send it to the task-executing model.

claims.about: rule shortlist plus a fine-tuned classifier; this sketch borrows the rule shortlist only and has no classifier
claims.quote: Rules shortlist relevant advice, and a lightweight 1.7B classifier fine-tuned on teacher-labeled state-suggestion pairs scores those candidates instead of generating a diagnosis.

claims.about: the micro-contract idea borrowed here (required arguments, valid options)
claims.quote: Micro-contracts encode reusable interface checks, such as required arguments or valid options, without prescribing complete task programs.

claims.about: the cooldown and token-budget idea borrowed here
claims.quote: A Prompt Value Table records earlier guidance and feedback to limit repeated suggestions through cooldown and token-budget checks.

claims.about: the authors' benchmark results (attempts, successes, gain over Base, replaced diagnosis calls, control-time reductions)
claims.quote: Across 1,308 attempts per method in AppWorld and WebShop, Synapse-Control achieves 270 successes (29.8% more than Base), replaces 4,987 generative diagnosis calls, and reduces auxiliary control time relative to Sentry by 50.2% and 51.0%, respectively.

not_results_of_this_sketch: All tools, contracts, advice, histories, budgets and times here are synthetic, hand-declared fixtures. The timeline counts printed by fixtures.py describe that fixture only; they say nothing about any agent, benchmark or the paper's system.
